newsitem.title: UK: Volume low on UK grain futures and physical market.
newsitem.headline: Volume low on UK grain futures and physical market.

text.p: LIFFE grains ended a subdued day's trading tightly mixed, while the UK physical grains market stayed quiet as farmers continued to hold on to available supplies.

On wheat, new crop months were holding above round numbers, one trader said. For November, the most active contract, this meant support at the day's low of 89.00 stg. It last traded at 89.15 stg, compared with the previous settlement of 89.25 stg.
Volume on November was 64 lots, of a total 118.

July accounted for most of the rest of the volume, with 48 lots done. It bottomed out, and then found some support from book squaring and profit taking, the trader said. July last traded 0.20 stg lower at 81.45 stg, compared with a low of 81.00 stg.
On barley, November was most active with 18 of 30 lots done. It last changed hands 0.15 stg lower at 84.35 stg.
The physical market was also quiet, with some traders blaming low prices for a lack of farmer selling, despite trade sentiment that on-farm supplies remain abundant.
"It's not happening today. It's too cheap," one country broker said.
"You can't persuade the farmers to sell," another said.
He felt farmers were ignoring the realities of a well supplied market. "The farmers have their heads in the sand," he said.
Brokers reported feed wheat done to east Anglia for July at 84.50 stg, with milling wheat going in the south midlands for 111.00 stg for June delivery.
